description: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 CAM board (57 x 28 mm, maker not named by the seller; WROOM-1 with octal PSRAM, two USB-C: native USB and a USB-UART bridge on GPIO43/44). Camera and SD pins are seller-stated and match the ESP32-S3-EYE. Not yet built, flashed or captured on physical hardware.

source_references.title: Seller listing, "ESP32-S3 Pinout" page
source_references.notes: Printed to PDF, on the bench 2026-11-01. The listing names no maker or URL. Pinout gives CAM_SIOD 4, CAM_SIOC 5, VSYNC 6, HREF 7, XCLK 15, PCLK 13, Y2-Y9 11/9/8/10/12/18/17/16, SD DATA 40 / CLK 39 / CMD 38, GPIO35-37 PSRAM (octal module), LED GPIO2, WS2812 GPIO48, GPIO3 JTAG-enable strap. Sold with OV2640 or OV5640. Flash size (8 or 16 MB) not stated.

camera.notes: Pins are the ESP32-S3-EYE map exactly, so clawcam_camera_default_esp32_s3_eye_config already drives this board; only vflip differs (the EYE mounts its sensor inverted, this board's orientation is unchecked). esp32-camera detects the sensor by PID, so every listed option works with the same pins. xclk_hz follows the EYE profile; not measured on this board.

motion.notes: No PIR on the board. Free GPIOs per the seller pinout: 1, 14, 21, 41, 42, 47. Set pir_gpio to whichever is wired before enabling motion wake.

power.notes: No battery input is documented; USB-powered. ADC-based battery estimates stay off.

promotion_requirements: ESP-IDF firmware builds with the esp32-camera component enabled.
Camera initializes and captures a valid JPEG frame on physical ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 CAM hardware, with the sensor it actually shipped with recorded here.
Image orientation is checked and vflip/hflip set to match.
Captured JPEG can be saved to the onboard MicroSD slot.
Gateway can ingest metadata generated from the hardware capture path.
Power and wake behavior are tested before enabling unattended field deployments.
